decision: Whether to replace CRA2 Gradio with Streamlit during Cloud Run preparation
decision_limits: No head-to-head implementation, security or effort measurements exist. A hosting capability cannot establish easier or blocker-free migration. Neither choice is deployment-ready on this evidence.

evidence.claim: Existing Gradio version has 337 passing Week 2-4 tests and nonroot Linux container proof: six offline workflows, config HTTP 200 on configured port and application-file HTTP 403. This is not deployed authentication or owner acceptance.

Fresh CI needs a reviewed reachable mirror of the same checksum-pinned encoder archive after the upstream URL returned 403. The encoder provisioning path does not depend on the UI framework. Inference: changing only the UI does not resolve that blocker.

An AST inventory of 80 Python files found four Gradio-importing files, zero Streamlit-importing files, and 11 consumers of week2.app. The app implements cooldown, trace selection/polling, clear/undo and session state; Slack and evaluation import its helpers. This is change-surface evidence, not a measured comparative effort result.
Google documents deploying a Streamlit application to Cloud Run. The example demonstrates hosting, not CRA2 feature parity or this application’s invited-user IAP acceptance.

Streamlit supports per-session state and access to initial request headers. Its documentation warns against using context.ip_address for security. Header access alone is not verified IAP identity or durable application storage.

IAP signed-header verification applies to all app types. Current plan still needs identity-scoped persistent state, release supply-chain controls and owner testing. These remain acceptance requirements with either UI.

flip_conditions: A concrete Gradio UI or authenticated transport blocker remains after a minimal repair, while a Streamlit slice passes the same acceptance checks.
A bounded Streamlit prototype demonstrates lower measured implementation effort without losing cooldown, trace privacy, session isolation, Slack or eval behavior.
The user explicitly changes the requirement from conditional framework flexibility to a mandatory Streamlit migration.

smallest_separating_test: Implement one isolated Streamlit chat slice using the same guarded workflow, cooldown and trace helpers. Exercise one normal and one refused request, two isolated sessions, clear/undo and trace display; compare required code changes and time with the existing Gradio baseline. If the disputed blocker is IAP transport, run the same owner-controlled allowed/denied-account and reconnect probe through IAP for both before claiming it is resolved.
